
{{alias}}( order, M, N, A, LDA, R, C, out )
    Computes row and column scale factors intended to equilibrate an M-by-N
    matrix `A` and reduce its condition number.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    The row scale factors are stored in `R` (which should have `M` indexed
    elements) and the column scale factors are stored in `C` (which should
    have `N` indexed elements).

    If the status code is zero, `R`, `C`, and all three elements of `out`
    contain valid values. If the status code is greater than `M`, `R`,
    `ROWCND`, and `AMAX` contain valid values, but `C` and `COLCND` do not.
    If the status code is greater than zero and less than or equal to `M`,
    only `AMAX` contains a valid value. Elements which do not contain valid
    values are left unmodified.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Row-major (C-style) or column-major (Fortran-style) order. Must be
        either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    M: integer
        Number of rows in `A`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix.

    LDA: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A` (a.k.a., leading dimension of
        the matrix `A`).

    R: Float64Array
        Output vector for the row scale factors.

    C: Float64Array
        Output vector for the column scale factors.

    out: Float64Array
        Three element output array whose elements are set to
        `[ ROWCND, COLCND, AMAX ]`, where `ROWCND` is the ratio of the
        smallest to the largest row scale factor, `COLCND` is the ratio of
        the smallest to the largest column scale factor, and `AMAX` is the
        absolute value of the largest element of `A`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. If zero, the scale factors were successfully computed.
        If greater than zero and less than or equal to `M`, the info-th row
        of `A` is exactly zero. If greater than `M`, the (info-M)-th column
        of `A` is exactly zero. Row and column indices are one-based,
        matching the LAPACK convention.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var out = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 2, 2, A, 2, R, C, out )
    0
    > R
    <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.25 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ ~1.3333, 1.0 ]
    > out
    <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.75, 4.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( M, N, A, sa1, sa2, oa, R, sr, or, C, sc, oc, out, so, oo )
    Computes row and column scale factors intended to equilibrate an M-by-N
    matrix `A` and reduce its condition number using alternative indexing
    semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    If the status code is zero, `R`, `C`, and all three elements of `out`
    contain valid values. If the status code is greater than `M`, `R`,
    `ROWCND`, and `AMAX` contain valid values, but `C` and `COLCND` do not.
    If the status code is greater than zero and less than or equal to `M`,
    only `AMAX` contains a valid value. Elements which do not contain valid
    values are left unmodified.

    Parameters
    ----------
    M: integer
        Number of rows in `A`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix.

    sa1: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A`.

    sa2: integer
        Stride of the second dimension of `A`.

    oa: integer
        Starting index for `A`.

    R: Float64Array
        Output vector for the row scale factors.

    sr: integer
        Stride length for `R`.

    or: integer
        Starting index for `R`.

    C: Float64Array
        Output vector for the column scale factors.

    sc: integer
        Stride length for `C`.

    oc: integer
        Starting index for `C`.

    out: Float64Array
        Three element output array whose elements are set to
        `[ ROWCND, COLCND, AMAX ]`.

    so: integer
        Stride length for `out`.

    oo: integer
        Starting index for `out`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. If zero, the scale factors were successfully computed.
        If greater than zero and less than or equal to `M`, the info-th row
        of `A` is exactly zero. If greater than `M`, the (info-M)-th column
        of `A` is exactly zero. Row and column indices are one-based,
        matching the LAPACK convention.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var out = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 2, 2, A, 2, 1, 0, R, 1, 0, C, 1, 0, out, 1, 0 )
    0
    > R
    <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.25 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ ~1.3333, 1.0 ]
    > out
    <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.75, 4.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
